title: Front-loop-only dc — FLO dc
subtitle: Work into the front loop only to leave a ridge on the back
excerpt: Front-loop-only dc inserts the hook into the front loop only of each stitch, leaving the back loop free. The free back loops form a visible ridge on the wrong side and create a slight crease on the right side. Standard for creating fold lines, horizontal stripes in colourwork, and light ribbing.

glossaryTerms.definition: Double crochet worked into the front loop only of each stitch. Abbreviated FLO dc. Leaves the back loop free as a visible horizontal ridge; used for fold lines, ribbing, and colourwork stripe definition.

heroPrompt: A crochet swatch in teal DK yarn showing alternating rows of standard dc and FLO dc, the horizontal ridges clearly visible, good side light, close-up.

inlineDiagramTopics.description: Hook inserted under the front loop only with back loop visible and free

content.text: works into one loop instead of two. Each double crochet top has a front loop (closest to you) and a back loop (away from you). FLO dc only uses the front loop, leaving the back loop as a raised strand across the fabric surface. A row of FLO dc produces a clear horizontal ridge that can be used as a fold line for bag bases, a colour-change crease, or a gentle rib across a garment yoke.
Work a foundation row of standard dc.
Ch 1, turn. Insert the hook into the front loop only of the first dc — the loop closest to you.
Complete the dc normally: yarn over, pull through the loop (2 loops on hook), yarn over, pull through both loops.
Continue FLO dc across the row. The back loops of the previous row are now visible as a ridge on the back (wrong side) of the work.

items.symptom: Can't tell the front loop from the back loop
items.cause: Looking at the stitch straight on without distinguishing which loop is nearest
items.fix: Hold the work flat. The front loop is the V-strand that angles toward you. The back loop is the strand that angles away. On a turned row after ch 1, the front loop is still toward you as you hold the work.

content.text: BLO dc is the mirror: inserting into the back loop only leaves the front loop free as a ridge on the right side. Alternating FLO and BLO rows creates a ribbed texture used in crochet ribbing bands and sleeve cuffs.
